title: Open neighborhoods with constant integral matrix coset
statement: Let K be a topological field, A an open subring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], Y a topological space, and g:Y → GL_n(K) have continuous entries and inverse entries. Every x has an open neighborhood W on which the right coset g(y)GL_n(A) equals g(x)GL_n(A). For the canonical finite p-adic coefficient extension its integer subring is open, since it contains the open unit ball.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; Open neighborhoods with constant integral matrix coset

proof.text: The integer subring contains the open ball of radius one about zero by its norm description. Translation makes it an open additive subgroup. Membership in the integral matrix subgroup is equivalent to integrality of every matrix and inverse entry.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), pp. 59–60; Open neighborhoods with constant integral matrix coset

proof.text: For fixed x, intersect the inverse images of A under all entries of g(x)⁻¹g(y) and g(y)⁻¹g(x). Finiteness makes this open; at x the entries form the identity and are integral. The two matrices are inverse, so the subgroup criterion gives equality of right cosets.
